questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of compound the Legumelin is?
questions.solution:
Legumelin is a type of albumin protein found in the seeds of leguminous plants.

Albumins are water-soluble proteins that are spherical or globular in shape.

Therefore, legumelin is classified as a globular protein.

Answer: Globular protein

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product when glucose reacts with bromine water.
questions.solution:
Bromine water is a mild oxidizing agent.

When glucose reacts with bromine water, the aldehyde group ($-CHO$) is oxidized to a carboxylic acid group ($-COOH$), while the hydroxyl groups remain unaffected.

The reaction is given by:

$CHO-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH + Br_2/H_2O \rightarrow COOH-(CHOH)_4-CH_2OH$

The product formed is gluconic acid.

Answer: Gluconic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of glycosidic bond is present in maltose?
questions.solution:
Maltose is a disaccharide composed of two $\alpha$-D-glucose units.

The two glucose units are linked together by an $\alpha$-1,4-glycosidic bond, which is formed between the C-1 of the first $\alpha$-D-glucose molecule and the C-4 of the second $\alpha$-D-glucose molecule.

Thus, the glycosidic bond present in maltose is $\alpha$-1, 4.

Answer: $\alpha\text{-}1, 4$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a natural source of ascorbic acid from following.
questions.solution:
Ascorbic acid is commonly known as Vitamin C.

Citrus fruits such as oranges, lemons, and grapefruits are rich natural sources of ascorbic acid.

Clove is a source of eugenol, wintergreen is a source of methyl salicylate, and cinnamon is a source of cinnamaldehyde.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amino acids is an essential amino acid ?
questions.solution:
Essential amino acids are those which cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained through diet.

The essential amino acids are Valine, Leucine, Isoleucine, Phenylalanine, Methionine, Tryptophan, Threonine, Lysine, Arginine, and Histidine.

Among the given options, Phenylalanine is an essential amino acid, while Tyrosine, Glutamine, and Alanine are non-essential amino acids.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following contains mainly saturated fats ?
questions.solution:
Margarine is produced by the catalytic hydrogenation of liquid vegetable oils, which converts the unsaturated fatty acids into saturated fatty acids to make it solid at room temperature. Therefore, it contains mainly saturated fats.

Olive oil, safflower oil, and fish oil are rich in unsaturated fats (monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats).

Answer: Margarine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amino acids has a unique structure so that the side chain connects to the back bone of amino acid at two points ?
questions.solution:
Proline is a unique amino acid because its side chain is bonded to both the $\alpha$-carbon and the amino group nitrogen, forming a cyclic pyrrolidine ring.

Due to this cyclic structure, the side chain connects to the backbone of the amino acid at two points.

Other given amino acids (Histidine, Tryptophan, Tyrosine) have side chains that connect only to the $\alpha$-carbon.

Answer: Proline

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following pairs of carbohydrates contains galactose in both of them as one of the constituent ?
questions.solution:
Lactose is a disaccharide which on hydrolysis yields one molecule of D-galactose and one molecule of D-glucose.

Raffinose is a trisaccharide which on hydrolysis yields one molecule each of D-galactose, D-glucose, and D-fructose.

Sucrose is a disaccharide yielding D-glucose and D-fructose on hydrolysis.

Maltose is a disaccharide yielding two molecules of D-glucose on hydrolysis.

Thus, both lactose and raffinose contain galactose as one of their constituent monosaccharides.

Answer: Lactose and Raffinose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following, sugar is an aldohexose?
questions.solution:
Glucose is a monosaccharide containing six carbon atoms and an aldehyde group. Thus, it is an aldohexose.

Ribose is an aldopentose.

Fructose is a ketohexose.

Lactose is a disaccharide.

Answer: Glucose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is classified as oligosaccharide?
questions.solution:
Carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units on hydrolysis are called oligosaccharides.

Sucrose is a disaccharide, which is a type of oligosaccharide, as it yields one molecule of glucose and one molecule of fructose on hydrolysis.

Ribose, fructose, and glucose are monosaccharides, as they cannot be hydrolyzed further into simpler units of polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a protein present in nails
questions.solution:
Keratin is a tough, fibrous structural protein that forms the main structural constituent of hair, feathers, hooves, claws, horns, and nails.

Legumelin is a protein found in leguminous plants.

Myosin is a motor protein found in muscles that is responsible for muscle contraction.

Insulin is a peptide hormone produced by the pancreas that regulates blood sugar levels.

Answer: Keratin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify glycosidic linkage in lactose.
questions.solution:
Lactose is a disaccharide composed of $\beta$-D-galactose and $\beta$-D-glucose.

The glycosidic linkage is formed between C1 of $\beta$-D-galactose and C4 of $\beta$-D-glucose.

Therefore, the glycosidic linkage in lactose is $\beta-1,4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total mass of products obtained when one gram mole of sucrose is hydrolysed?
questions.solution:
The chemical equation for the hydrolysis of sucrose is:

$C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} + H_2O \rightarrow C_6H_{12}O_6 + C_6H_{12}O_6$

One mole of sucrose reacts with one mole of water to produce one mole of glucose and one mole of fructose.

Molar mass of glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) = $180\ \text{g/mol}$

Molar mass of fructose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) = $180\ \text{g/mol}$

Total mass of products = $180 + 180 = 360\ \text{g}$

Answer: $360\ \text{g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has largest size?
questions.solution:
The size of the given biological entities generally follows the order: Antibody < Virus < Bacteria < Cancer cell.

Antibodies are protein molecules and are the smallest (around $10$ to $15$ nm).

Viruses are infectious agents composed of genetic material and protein coats, typically ranging from $20$ to $300$ nm.

Bacteria are prokaryotic cells, usually measuring between $1$ to $10\mu$m.

Cancer cells are eukaryotic animal cells, which are the largest among the given options, typically ranging from $10$ to $30\mu$m or more.

Therefore, a cancer cell has the largest size.

Answer: Cancer cell

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is NOT a globular protein?
questions.solution:
Proteins are classified into two types based on their molecular shape: fibrous proteins and globular proteins.

Fibrous proteins have a thread-like structure. Examples include keratin (present in hair, wool, silk) and myosin (present in muscles).

Globular proteins have a spherical shape. Examples include insulin, egg albumin, and serum albumin.

Therefore, keratin is a fibrous protein and not a globular protein.

Answer: Keratin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following enzymes cleaves glycosidic bond in sucrose?
questions.solution:
Sucrose is a disaccharide composed of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-fructose linked by a glycosidic bond.

The enzyme invertase catalyzes the hydrolysis of sucrose into its constituent monosaccharides, glucose and fructose. This process is also known as the inversion of cane sugar.

Amylose is a polysaccharide, not an enzyme. Trypsin is a proteolytic enzyme that cleaves peptide bonds in proteins. Maltase is an enzyme that hydrolyzes maltose into two glucose molecules.

Answer: Invertase

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a protein of muscles ?
questions.solution:
Myosin is a motor protein that, along with actin, forms the contractile filaments of muscle cells.

Keratin is a structural protein found in hair, nails, and skin.

Legumelin is a plant protein found in legumes.

Insulin is a peptide hormone produced by the pancreas.

Thus, myosin is the protein of muscles.

Answer: Myosin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify medicinaly important compound extracted from citrus fruits?
questions.solution:
Citrus fruits such as oranges, lemons, and grapefruits are rich natural sources of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

Vitamin C is a medicinally important compound that acts as an antioxidant, helps in the synthesis of collagen, and prevents scurvy.

Antimicrobials, analgesics, and antiseptics are broad classes of medicinal drugs and are not specifically extracted from citrus fruits.

Answer: Vit. C

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following oils is mainly a saturated fats?
questions.solution:
Saturated fats are typically solid at room temperature and contain single bonds between carbon atoms in their fatty acid chains.

Coconut oil is composed of approximately $80\%$ to $90\%$ saturated fat, primarily lauric acid, myristic acid, and palmitic acid.

Olive oil is mainly composed of monounsaturated fats (oleic acid).

Safflower oil and fish oil are rich in polyunsaturated fats (such as linoleic acid and omega-3 fatty acids, respectively).

Therefore, coconut oil is mainly a saturated fat.

Answer: Coconut oil

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amino acids does NOT contain chiral carbon?
questions.solution:
The general structure of an $\alpha$-amino acid is $H_{2}N-CH(R)-COOH$.

For an amino acid to be chiral, the $\alpha$-carbon must be attached to four different groups.

In glycine, the side chain $R$ is a hydrogen atom ($H$).

The structure of glycine is $H_{2}N-CH_{2}-COOH$.

Since the $\alpha$-carbon is attached to two identical hydrogen atoms, it does not have four different groups attached to it, making it achiral.

Valine, alanine, and isoleucine have different $R$ groups (isopropyl, methyl, and sec-butyl respectively) and thus contain chiral carbons.

Answer: Glycine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which carbon atom (numbered from 1' to 5') of ribose lacks the oxygen to form deoxyribose ?
questions.solution:
Ribose and deoxyribose are pentose sugars found in RNA and DNA respectively.

The structure of ribose has a hydroxyl group (-OH) attached to the 2' carbon atom.

In deoxyribose, the 2' carbon atom has only a hydrogen atom (-H) attached to it, lacking the oxygen atom present in ribose.

Thus, the 2' carbon atom of ribose lacks the oxygen to form deoxyribose.

Answer: 2'

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is used to prepare adipic acid, enzymatically in Green technology developed by Darth and Frost?
questions.solution:
In the green technology developed by Draths and Frost, adipic acid is synthesized using D-glucose as the starting material.

The process involves the use of genetically engineered bacteria (E. coli) to convert glucose into cis,cis-muconic acid through a biocatalytic pathway. The cis,cis-muconic acid is subsequently hydrogenated under mild conditions to produce adipic acid.

This method provides an environmentally friendly alternative to the traditional synthesis of adipic acid, which relies on petroleum-based benzene and generates nitrous oxide (a greenhouse gas) as a byproduct.

Answer: Glucose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is found to raise the HDL level in the blood?
questions.solution:
Omega-3 fatty acids are polyunsaturated fatty acids that are known to increase the level of High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL), which is considered good cholesterol, in the blood. They also help in lowering triglyceride levels, thereby reducing the risk of cardiovascular diseases.

Trans fats, on the other hand, lower HDL levels and raise LDL (bad cholesterol) levels.

Answer: Omega-3 fatty acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The letter 'D' in carbohydrates signifies
questions.solution:
The letters 'D' and 'L' before the name of carbohydrates represent the relative configuration of the molecule with respect to glyceraldehyde.

It does not indicate the optical activity (dextrorotatory or laevorotatory), which is represented by (+) or (-) signs respectively.

Therefore, 'D' signifies configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules is capable of forming Zwitter ion?
questions.solution:
A Zwitter ion is a dipolar ion formed by the internal transfer of a proton from an acidic group to a basic group within the same molecule.

Among the given options, $\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (glycine) is an amino acid that contains both an acidic carboxyl group ($-\text{COOH}$) and a basic amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$).

In aqueous solution, the $-\text{COOH}$ group donates a proton to the $-\text{NH}_2$ group, forming the Zwitter ion $^{+}\text{NH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^{-}$.

The other molecules lack either an acidic or a basic group required for this internal proton transfer.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ionic species is present in hemoglobin and responsible for transformation of oxygen ?
questions.solution:
Hemoglobin is an iron-containing metalloprotein found in red blood cells, responsible for the transport of oxygen in the body.

The central metal ion in the heme group of hemoglobin is iron (specifically $\text{Fe}^{+2}$ in its active state). Among the given options, the iron species is the correct choice.

Answer: $\text{Fe}^{+3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the linkage in backbone of single strand of DNA ?
questions.solution:
The backbone of a single strand of DNA is formed by alternating sugar and phosphate molecules.

The nitrogenous bases are attached to the sugar molecules and project outwards from the backbone, meaning they are not part of the continuous backbone chain.

Thus, the continuous chain forming the backbone consists of phosphate-sugar-phosphate linkages.

Answer: Phosphate -sugar-phosphate

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the natural source of ascorbic acid from following.
questions.solution:
Ascorbic acid is commonly known as Vitamin C.

Citrus fruits such as oranges, lemons, and amla are rich natural sources of ascorbic acid.

Cinnamon, turmeric, and clove are spices and do not serve as primary sources of ascorbic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During denaturation, which level of protein structure remains unchanged?
questions.solution:
Denaturation of a protein involves the disruption of its secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structures due to the breaking of non-covalent interactions such as hydrogen bonds, hydrophobic interactions, and disulfide bridges.

The primary structure, which is the sequence of amino acids linked by strong covalent peptide bonds, is not affected by denaturation and remains intact.

Answer: primary

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct?
A) $\alpha$ - amino acids present in protein is L- amino acid.
B) Amino acids contain $\text{NH}_2$ as well as COOH group.
C) Number of amino group and carboxylic group are same in amino acids always.
D) Tryosine was firstly obtained from cheese.
Choose the correct alternatives from below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. Naturally occurring $\alpha$-amino acids present in proteins have the L-configuration.

Statement B is correct. Amino acids are organic compounds containing both an amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$) and a carboxylic acid group ($-\text{COOH}$).

Statement C is incorrect. The number of amino and carboxylic groups can vary. Acidic amino acids have more carboxylic groups than amino groups, whereas basic amino acids have more amino groups than carboxylic groups.

Statement D is correct. Tyrosine was first isolated from casein, a protein found in cheese. Its name is derived from the Greek word 'tyros', meaning cheese.

Therefore, statements A, B, and D are correct.

Answer: A, B and D only

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is confirmed by the reaction of glucose with hydroxylamine?
options: Straight chain of six carbon atoms
questions.solution:
Glucose reacts with hydroxylamine ($NH_2OH$) to form an oxime.

This reaction is a characteristic property of aldehydes and ketones, which confirms the presence of a carbonyl group ($\gt C=O$) in the glucose molecule.

The reaction with hydrogen iodide ($HI$) confirms the straight chain of six carbon atoms, while oxidation with nitric acid confirms the primary alcoholic group.

Answer: Carbonyl group

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which component of DNA carries genetic information?
questions.solution:
The genetic information in DNA is stored in the specific sequence of its nitrogenous bases (adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine).

The sugar and phosphate groups form the structural backbone of the DNA molecule, while hydrogen bonds hold the two complementary strands together.

Therefore, the sequence of nitrogenous bases is responsible for carrying genetic information.

Answer: Sequence of nitrogenous bases

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds forms starch on polymerization?
questions.solution:
Starch is a polysaccharide composed of two components: amylose and amylopectin.

Both amylose and amylopectin are polymers of $\alpha$-D-glucose.

Amylose is a linear polymer with C1-C4 glycosidic linkages, while amylopectin is a branched polymer with C1-C4 and C1-C6 glycosidic linkages.

Therefore, starch is formed by the polymerization of $\alpha$-D-glucose.

Answer: $\alpha$-D-glucose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the correct sequence of the complementary strand for the given portion of a DNA molecule:- 5' - G A C G T A C -3' ?
options: 3' - T T G C A T G - 5'
3' - C T G C A T C - 5'
3' - C T G C A T G - 5'
3' - C T G T A T G - 5'
questions.solution:
According to the base pairing rules in DNA, Adenine (A) pairs with Thymine (T) and Guanine (G) pairs with Cytosine (C).

The two strands of DNA are antiparallel, meaning the 5' end of one strand pairs with the 3' end of the complementary strand.

Given sequence: 5' - G A C G T A C - 3'

Complementary sequence: 3' - C T G C A T G - 5'

Answer: 3' - C T G C A T G - 5'

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the cation present in chlorophyll in green plants.
questions.solution:
Chlorophyll is a green pigment found in plants, algae, and cyanobacteria, which is essential for photosynthesis.

Structurally, chlorophyll is a coordination complex consisting of a substituted porphyrin ring (specifically a chlorin ring) with a central metal ion.

The central metal ion coordinated in the porphyrin ring of chlorophyll is magnesium, specifically in the $+2$ oxidation state.

Thus, the cation present in chlorophyll is $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.

Answer: $\text{Mg}^{2+}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one of the following is a globular protein?
questions.solution:
Proteins are classified into fibrous and globular proteins based on their molecular shape.

Fibrous proteins have a fiber-like structure formed by parallel polypeptide chains held together by hydrogen and disulfide bonds. Examples include keratin (found in hair, wool, silk) and myosin (found in muscles).

Globular proteins have a spherical shape formed when the chains of polypeptides coil around. Examples include insulin and albumins.

Thus, insulin is a globular protein.

Answer: Insulin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which carbon atoms of glucose, numbered from 1 to 6 forms a hemiacetal structure between -CHO and -OH groups.?
questions.solution:
In the open-chain structure of glucose, the aldehyde group (-CHO) is present at C-1.

The cyclic hemiacetal structure is formed by the intramolecular nucleophilic addition of the -OH group at C-5 to the -CHO group at C-1.

This results in the formation of a stable six-membered pyranose ring.

Thus, the -OH group at C-5 is involved in the hemiacetal formation.

Answer: C-5

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of saccharide the maltose is?
questions.solution:
Maltose is a carbohydrate that yields two molecules of $\alpha$-D-glucose upon hydrolysis.

The two glucose units are linked together by an $\alpha(1 \rightarrow 4)$ glycosidic bond.

Since it is composed of two monosaccharide units, maltose is classified as a disaccharide.

Answer: Disaccharide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The secondary structure of protein is determined by
questions.solution:
The secondary structure of a protein refers to the shape in which a long polypeptide chain can exist.

They are found to exist in two different types of structures, namely $\alpha$-helix and $\beta$-pleated sheet structures.

These structures arise due to the regular folding of the backbone of the polypeptide chain due to hydrogen bonding between the $-\text{C}=\text{O}$ and $-\text{NH}-$ groups of the peptide bonds.

Therefore, the secondary structure of a protein is determined by hydrogen bonds.

Answer: hydrogen bond

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The reaction of glucose with acetic Anhydride, confirms the
questions.solution:
Glucose reacts with acetic anhydride to form glucose pentaacetate.

The formation of the pentaacetate derivative indicates that there are five hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) groups present in a molecule of glucose.

Since glucose is a stable compound, these five hydroxyl groups must be attached to five different carbon atoms.

Answer: presence of five hydroxyl group

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following statements is NOT correct regarding tannins?
options: These avoid browning of freshly cut potato.
These are obtained by polymerisation of quinones.
These are generated after cutting fruits or vegetables.
questions.solution:
The browning process in plant tissues involves tannins and related phenolic compounds. When cells are damaged, enzymes oxidize these phenolics to quinones, which then polymerize into melanins. This mechanism indicates tannins are contributors to browning, not preventatives.

Tannins are polyphenolic compounds formed biosynthetically from simpler phenolic precursors, not from polymerization of quinones. Quinones are instead products of tannin oxidation during browning.

These compounds exist naturally in plant tissues prior to cutting; they are not generated afterward. Cutting merely releases them, facilitating enzymatic reactions.

Among the options, C inaccurately describes tannins as polymers of quinones, contradicting their true chemical nature and biosynthesis.

The correct identification is: $\boxed{C}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify a side chain $(R)$ group present in Leucine, an amino acid.
questions.solution:
The side chain (R group) of leucine is an isobutyl group with structural formula $\mathrm{Me}_2\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-$.

Comparing the options:
A) $\mathrm{H}-$ (glycine)
B) $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ (alanine)
C) $\mathrm{Me}_2\mathrm{CH}-$ (valine)
D) $\mathrm{Me}_2\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ (leucine)

The isobutyl group corresponds to option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following carbohydrates produces glucose, galactose and fructose on hydrolysis?
questions.solution:
Raffinose hydrolyzes to yield glucose, galactose, and fructose. As a trisaccharide, its hydrolysis reaction is $\text{Raffinose} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Galactose} + \text{Fructose}$.

Maltose gives only glucose: $\text{Maltose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{Glucose}$. Cellulose produces glucose monomers: $(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5)_n + n\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow n\text{Glucose}$. Lactose yields glucose and galactose: $\text{Lactose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Galactose}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following molecules serves as fibrous content of food only and useful for bowel movement in humans?
questions.solution:
Dietary fiber refers to indigestible polysaccharides that provide bulk for bowel function. Amylopectin, amylose, and glycogen are all digestible by human enzymes and serve as energy sources, not solely as fiber.

Cellulose, composed of glucose units linked by $\beta$-1,4-glycosidic bonds, cannot be hydrolyzed due to the absence of cellulase in humans. It passes through the digestive tract undigested, adding bulk to stool and facilitating bowel movements.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following nitrogen bases of nucleic acids is derived from purine?
questions.solution: No Solution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the carbon atom numbered from $\mathrm{C}_1{ }^{\prime}$ to $\mathrm{C}_5{ }^{\prime}$ of monosaccharide unit of DNA nucleotide that lacks oxygen atom from -OH group.
questions.solution:
The monosaccharide unit in DNA is deoxyribose, a pentose sugar distinguished from ribose by the absence of oxygen at the C-2′ position.
Ribose contains a hydroxyl group (-OH) at C-2′, whereas deoxyribose substitutes this with a hydrogen atom (-H).
All other carbon atoms (C-1′, C-3′, C-4′, C-5′) either include oxygen in hydroxyl groups, the furanose ring, or participate in glycosidic or phosphodiester bonds.

$\boxed{B}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify acidic amino acid from following list represented by three letter symbols.
questions.solution:
Amino acids are classified based on their side chain properties as neutral (polar or non-polar), acidic, or basic. Among the given options:

Threonine has a polar hydroxyl group, making it neutral polar. Tryptophan's indole ring classifies it as neutral non-polar. Histidine contains an imidazole group that can accept protons, classifying it as basic.

Glutamic acid possesses an additional carboxyl group in its side chain that donates protons, making it acidic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify neutral aminoacid from following list represented by three letter symbols.
questions.solution:
Amino acid classification depends on the properties of their side chains. Basic amino acids contain proton-accepting groups, acidic amino acids contain proton-donating carboxyl groups, and neutral amino acids lack ionizable groups in their side chains.

Arginine features a guanidinium group that protonates at physiological pH, classifying it as basic. Aspartic acid contains an additional carboxylic acid group, making it acidic. Leucine has a nonpolar aliphatic side chain without ionizable groups, rendering it neutral. Histidine's imidazole ring can accept protons near physiological pH, classifying it as basic.

Among these, only leucine lacks acidic or basic character in its side chain.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What are the positions of ' N ' atoms present in purine ring of nucleic acids?
questions.solution:
The purine ring system consists of a pyrimidine ring fused to an imidazole ring with standardized nitrogen positions at 1, 3, 7, and 9.

The pyrimidine ring contributes nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3; the imidazole ring contributes nitrogen atoms at positions 7 and 9. Position 5 is occupied by a carbon atom.

Comparing with the options:

A) 1,3 and 5 – incorrect due to carbon at position 5

B) 1,3 and 9 – omits position 7

C) 1,5,7 and 9 – includes carbon position 5

D) 1,3,7 and 9 – matches all nitrogen positions correctly

The correct nitrogen positions correspond to option D.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of glycosidic linkages are present in amylose?
questions.solution:
Amylose consists of D-glucose units connected by $\alpha$-$1,4$ glycosidic bonds, where the anomeric carbon (C-1) of one glucose is linked to C-4 of the adjacent unit in the $\alpha$ configuration.
While amylopectin features both $\alpha$-$1,4$ and $\alpha$-$1,6$ glycosidic linkages, and cellulose contains $\beta$-$1,4$ glycosidic linkages, amylose is uniquely characterized by $\alpha$-$1,4$ glycosidic bonds.

Final Answer: A. $\alpha$-$1,4$ glycosidic linkages

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of carbon atoms present in a sugar molecule of RNA nucleotide?
questions.solution:
An RNA nucleotide contains a ribose pentose sugar. As a pentose, it consists of five carbon atoms, conventionally labeled C1′, C2′, C3′, C4′, and C5′.

Therefore, there are $5$ carbon atoms in the RNA sugar molecule.

The answer is option B.

questions.solution: No Solution

questions.q: Identify glycosidic linkage in maltose.
questions.solution:
Maltose is a disaccharide composed of two $\alpha$-D-glucose units connected by an $\alpha$-1,4-glycosidic bond.

This indicates that the anomeric C1 carbon of one $\alpha$-D-glucose molecule forms a glycosidic linkage to the C4 carbon of the adjacent glucose unit, with the bond configuration being $\alpha$.

Correct answer: A. $\alpha$-1,4

questions.solution:
Amino acids are classified based on their side chain properties as neutral (polar or non-polar), acidic, or basic. Among the given options:

Threonine has a polar hydroxyl group, making it neutral polar. Tryptophan's indole ring classifies it as neutral non-polar. Histidine contains an imidazole group that can accept protons, classifying it as basic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of -OH groups present in a nucleoside involved in formation of DNA?
questions.solution:
A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base and a pentose sugar. In DNA, the pentose is 2′-deoxyribose, which differs from ribose by the absence of a hydroxyl group at the 2′ position.

The hydroxyl groups in 2′-deoxyribose are as follows: the 1′ carbon is bonded to the nitrogenous base and lacks a free $\mathrm{-OH}$, the 2′ carbon has a hydrogen atom ($\mathrm{-H}$) instead of $\mathrm{-OH}$, the 3′ carbon has a hydroxyl group, the 4′ carbon is part of the ring structure without a free $\mathrm{-OH}$, and the 5′ carbon has a hydroxyl group.

Thus, a 2′-deoxyribonucleoside has two hydroxyl groups: one at the 3′ position and one at the 5′ position.

$\boxed{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of -OH groups present in ribonucleoside?
questions.solution:
A ribonucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base attached to the ribose sugar at the C1' carbon via an N-glycosidic bond.

The β-D-ribofuranose form of ribose contains hydroxyl groups at positions C1', C2', C3', and C5'. During nucleoside formation, the hydroxyl at C1' is replaced by the nitrogenous base, leaving hydroxyl groups at C2', C3', and C5'.

$\boxed{3}$

questions.q: What type of glycosidic linkages are present in cellulose?
questions.solution: No Solution

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which amino acid from following contains $-\mathrm{CH}_3$ as side chain ?
questions.solution:

The methyl group ($-\mathrm{CH}_3$) appears as the R-group in alanine.

questions.solution:
The nitrogenous base thymine is characterized by a pyrimidine ring with a methyl group at position 5 and two carbonyl groups at positions 2 and 4, but lacks an $\mathrm{NH}_2$ group.

In contrast, adenine and guanine (purines) and cytosine (a pyrimidine) all contain amino groups at positions 6, 2, and 4, respectively.

Therefore, the base lacking an $\mathrm{NH}_2$ group is thymine.

The final answer is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.solution:
The presence of a heterocyclic ring in an amino acid side chain requires examining structural features beyond aliphatic or simple functional groups.

Threonine's side chain $\mathrm{-CH(OH)CH_3}$ is purely aliphatic with hydroxyl substitution. Cysteine's $\mathrm{-CH_2SH}$ contains a thiol group without cyclic structure. Valine's $\mathrm{-CH(CH_3)_2}$ is a branched alkyl chain.

Histidine possesses an imidazole ring $\mathrm{-CH_2}$-imidazole as its side chain, featuring a five-membered aromatic heterocycle with two nitrogen atoms.

Only histidine contains a heterocyclic ring system, making it the correct identification.

questions.q: Which from following on hydrolysis forms invert sugar?
questions.solution:
The hydrolysis of sucrose yields an equimolar mixture of D-(+)-glucose and D-(-)-fructose, known as invert sugar due to the inversion of optical rotation from positive (sucrose) to negative (fructose).

The reaction proceeds as: $\text{Sucrose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{H}^+ \text{ or invertase}} \text{D-(+)-Glucose} + \text{D-(-)-Fructose}$.

This confirms that sucrose hydrolysis produces invert sugar.

The correct identification is $\boxed{A}$.

questions.q: Which carbon atom of glucopyranose numbered from $\mathrm{C}-1$ to $\mathrm{C}-6$ is anomeric?
questions.solution:
The anomeric carbon in cyclic sugars originates from the carbonyl carbon in the open-chain form. In glucose, an aldohexose, the aldehyde group is located at $\mathrm{C}-1$.

During cyclization to form glucopyranose, the $\mathrm{C}-1$ aldehyde carbon reacts with the hydroxyl group at $\mathrm{C}-5$, forming a hemiacetal. This positions $\mathrm{C}-1$ as bonded to both the ring oxygen and the anomeric hydroxyl group.

$\mathrm{C}-1$ becomes chiral upon ring formation and serves as the anomeric carbon.

The correct identification is $\mathrm{D}$.

questions.solution:
The chemical formula of glucose is C6H12O6, indicating 6 carbon atoms per molecule.

For 0.35 mole of glucose, the number of molecules is $0.35 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 2.1077 \times 10^{23}$.

The total carbon atoms are then $2.1077 \times 10^{23} \times 6 = 1.26462 \times 10^{24}$, matching option C.

To identify the neutral amino acid, consider the side chain properties of each option.

Arginine (Arg) contains a guanidinium group that is protonated and positively charged, while lysine (Lys) has a primary amino group that also carries a positive charge.

Glutamic acid (Glu) features an additional carboxyl group that is deprotonated and negatively charged.

Tryptophan is therefore the neutral amino acid among these options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following tests confirms presence of aldehydic group in glucose ?
options: Formation of oxime when reacted with $\mathrm{NH}_2 \mathrm{OH}$.
Formation of gluconic acid when reacted with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ water.
Formation of saccharic acid when glucose and gluconic acid treated with dil $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ -
Formation of penta acetate when treated with acetic anhydride.
questions.solution:
Identifying the aldehyde group in glucose requires a test specific to aldehydes that distinguishes them from ketones. Glucose contains both an aldehyde and multiple hydroxyl groups.

Bromine water ($\mathrm{Br}_2$) serves as a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes the aldehyde group ($\mathrm{-CHO}$) to a carboxylic acid ($\mathrm{-COOH}$), forming gluconic acid. Ketones remain unaffected by this reagent, making this reaction specific for aldehydes.

While hydroxylamine ($\mathrm{NH}_2\mathrm{OH}$) forms an oxime with carbonyl groups, it reacts with both aldehydes and ketones, confirming only the presence of a carbonyl group rather than specifically an aldehyde.

Dilute nitric acid ($\mathrm{HNO}_3$) oxidizes both the aldehyde and primary alcohol groups to carboxylic acids, producing saccharic acid, so it is not specific to the aldehyde alone.

Acetic anhydride acetylates hydroxyl groups to form penta acetate, confirming only the presence of hydroxyl groups, not the aldehyde.

The formation of gluconic acid with bromine water provides the specific confirmation of an aldehydic group in glucose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following pairs of carbohydrates produce equal quantity of glucose on hydrolysis per mole?
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of carbohydrates releases constituent monosaccharides, with glucose yield depending on molecular structure.

Sucrose hydrolyzes to glucose and fructose: Sucrose + H2O → Glucose + Fructose, yielding 1 mole glucose per mole sucrose.

Lactose hydrolyzes to galactose and glucose: Lactose + H2O → Galactose + Glucose, yielding 1 mole glucose per mole lactose.

Maltose, composed of two glucose units, hydrolyzes to two glucose molecules: Maltose + H2O → 2 Glucose, yielding 2 moles glucose per mole maltose.

Raffinose hydrolyzes to galactose, glucose, and fructose: Raffinose + 2H2O → Galactose + Glucose + Fructose, yielding 1 mole glucose per mole raffinose.

Comparing yields: Sucrose and lactose both produce 1 mole glucose per mole carbohydrate, while maltose produces 2 moles. Raffinose produces 1 mole but differs from maltose.

The pair with equal glucose yield per mole is A) Sucrose and Lactose.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following carbohydrates produces double quantity of glucose on hydrolysis per mole as compared with sucrose?
questions.solution:
Sucrose undergoes hydrolysis to produce one mole of glucose per mole of sucrose: $\text{Sucrose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Fructose}$.

Evaluating the options:
Lactose yields one glucose: $\text{Lactose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Galactose}$.
Raffinose yields one glucose: $\text{Raffinose} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Fructose} + \text{Galactose}$.
Stachyose yields one glucose: $\text{Stachyose} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2\text{ Galactose} + \text{Glucose} + \text{Fructose}$.
Maltose yields two glucose: $\text{Maltose} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glucose} + \text{Glucose}$.

Maltose provides double the glucose per mole compared to sucrose.

Answer: $\boxed{\text{D}}$

An amino acid has the general structure $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{N}–\mathrm{CHR}–\mathrm{COOH}$, where R represents the side chain. For serine, the side chain is the hydroxymethyl group, $–\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}$.

D) $\mathrm{HO}–\mathrm{CH}_2–$ (equivalent to $–\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}$) matches serine

The correct representation of serine's R group is therefore option D.

questions.solution:
A triglyceride contains three ester linkages, each requiring one water molecule for hydrolysis. The stoichiometry of complete hydrolysis shows that one mole of triglyceride consumes three moles of water.

$\text{Triglyceride} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Glycerol} + 3\text{Fatty Acids}$

For n moles of triglyceride, the water requirement scales linearly as $3\text{n}$ moles.

Final answer: $\boxed{3\text{n}}$

The answer is $\boxed{C}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of glycosidic linkages are developed when excess glucose is to be stored for future use in animals?
questions.solution:
In animals, excess glucose is stored as glycogen, a polysaccharide that serves as a form of energy reserve. Glycogen is made up of glucose molecules connected by glycosidic linkages, and it has a highly branched structure.
- Alpha-1,4 glycosidic linkages connect glucose units in the linear chain of glycogen. These linkages form between the hydroxyl group on carbon 1 of one glucose molecule and the hydroxyl group on carbon 4 of the next glucose molecule.
- Alpha-1,6 glycosidic linkages occur at the branch points of the glycogen molecule. These linkages form between the hydroxyl group on carbon 1 of one glucose molecule and the hydroxyl group on carbon 6 of another glucose molecule, creating the branches.

questions.q: Which from following is NOT a globular protein?

Classification of proteins into globular and fibrous types depends on shape and solubility characteristics. Globular proteins exhibit spherical morphology, compact folding, and aqueous solubility, while fibrous proteins display elongated structures, mechanical functions, and water insolubility.

Evaluating the options: Legumelin serves as a storage protein with globular characteristics; egg albumin demonstrates classical globular properties with high solubility; insulin functions as a compact hormonal protein with globular conformation.

Myosin functions as the motor protein in muscle contraction, featuring an elongated fibrous tail domain that assembles into insoluble filaments. Despite possessing a globular head region, its primary classification derives from its fibrous structural role.

Thus, myosin represents the non-globular protein among the options.
